markers.reading: The party is hosted at the waystation; Delwath goes to the common room to gather Darba news, and the DM includes the others in the attention there.

evidence.quote: So she kind of busies herself a little bit and gets you settled in some rooms and then heads back to sort of spread the news of the opening of the road. And of course you're welcome to take your food in your rooms or head to the common room as you'd like.

What's it like there? Who's the— who are the important people? You know where's the good inns? Where's the dangerous parts of town? You know, just anything, any kind of intel we can gather on. markers.reading: The continuing journey from the inn reaches Darba’s gates; after the coastal approach, the closing narration takes the party through them.

evidence.quote: What's the what's the landscape like is it like a city on a flat plain it's on the water too and on the ocean or?
On the coast, yeah. Yo, yo, so it—so the land is much, much hillier, and it's on a river, actually. Um— you know, as you pass as you sort of cross through the you know, as you cross…

Plains here, and and sort of come—the Yuvanti Mountains are sort of creeping up to the south here, and as you come to this gap in the mountains, so, if you look at the map, you can see that, like, as you approach, as you approach Darba, there's sort of gap between the two mountain chains, the north and south, because of the Yuvanti Mountains are to the south.

And as you sort of come into this gap, the climate becomes much wetter. There's sort of rivers. There's forests. Small forest, patchy forests, but still much more forests. There's no forest in central Dunmar. Even the area that you're sort of passing through here is— is not—

You know it's rockier there's like pockets of these monsoon forests and then there's like river gorges and sort of sheltered valleys that are dry up in the in the dry season and then turn into waterfalls and, you know, cascading rivers in the wet season. The, you know, the the river floors flood and then, you know, people tend to move up elevation in the wet season, down elevation in the dry season.

Rudhan River is the main river that flows past Darba, and it has many small tributaries, and the headwaters are not far from this inn, actually. Once you keep going—when you keep going west about— I don't know, about half the journey west, you'll come to them. Half the distance between here and Darba, you come to the headwaters of the Rudhan, and the and the road sort of follows the river, I'm—much of the rest of the way, although tending to stick to the higher ground, not down in the river valley itself.

And you get into a much more lush landscape, as you approach the coast sort of like um you know cliffs with with trees sort of grown up the cliffs and then waterfalls cascading down here kind of like…

But yeah, there's definitely a lot more trees as you as you cross across the sort of Yuvanti gap, the Yuvanti gap towards the coastal plain, as you as the, you know, you're descending an elevation to, off the high plateaus of central Dunmar.

Still raining the monsoon season is still quite robust, right? It rains almost every afternoon. All the rivers are in flood, the streams are full, the roads are kind of a mess, although once you get on the old Drankorian road, that road is in pretty good shape. A lot of people travel by boat, but you can't go far by boat because there's the rivers all cascade down these waterfalls so you can often not cannot go more than a day's journey by boat.

There's just a lot that, you know—there's a lot more economic diversity here. There's more agricultural diversity. You know, central Dunmar's basically horses and then it's small handful of crops in the river valleys that can be supported by irrigation. You've got—right here you've got timber. You've got, you know, diverse, diversified agriculture. You've got cattle and and as well as sheep and goats, which are the things common on the plains. Fewer horses, a lot more more boats. You know, there's a lot more wood to make boats than there is in central Dunmar. Wood is precious commodity.
The land just feels more richer and lusher than the Highlands is you sort of head down and down the coast to the Darba itself.

So, I mean, this is a combination, I guess, of both the rumors and information you get, but also a bit of a narration of the journey itself, right? So, hey, I'm— let's just say what What else do you want to look at in the mirror?

So after, you know, about 10 days on the road from the inn where you rejoin civilization, as you've approached these increasingly densely populated and civilized areas, I'm— you find yourself on the afternoon of some time in early August—will have the exact date once I calculate out stuff— about approaching the walled city of Darba in the late afternoon as the rains have cleared and the sun has come out behind the clouds.

Set on a rocky coastline, perched above the flooded swamps of the Rudhan River, as it at its river mouth, as it flows into the sea. And as you for a few hours now, you've come around sort of over over a rise and have been looking out at the ocean which…

Old trade road you're on follows the sort of height of the land north of the river, and the city itself is all pretty much set north of the river, I'm—avoiding this sort of river delta area and approaching the old gates, the Drankorian gates. Wrought iron motifs of confronted lions framing the gate visible even from a distance of nearly a mile.
So you have many destinations, and I'll remind you have all this when you play next. So— the— so we'll stop as you step through the gates and decide where to go next.

duration.basis: DM gives approximate actual journey from the inn at u1167–u1171

route.reading: Passes the gap near the Yuvanti Mountains into wetter, more wooded country.
Reaches the Rudhan headwaters and follows the river on the higher old road.
Approaches Darba north of the flooded river delta; passes villages, fields and mills without separate played stops.

markers.note: The geographical account is explicitly a mix of travelers’ information and journey narration. Arrival through the gates is established only by the final u1247–u1249 transition, after the historical vision.

markers.reading: On the Darba approach, the party sees the Illorian district across the flooded river, outside the city walls.

evidence.quote: The city itself, though, even outside the walls, is pretty densely settled, right? So there's a, like, shanty town of wooden dwellings and flooded muddy streets on the south side of the river. Now, in the monsoon flood there's small boats that are you can see in the distance going back and forth from the sort of main harbor on the North side to the sort of more informal harbor on the South side.

Many of these are distinctive high-prowed Illorian-hulled boats that that form of ferry service going back and forth. And this, you've heard people tell this: outside the walls to the south of the river is really that often the Illorian district. It's where a lot of Illorians, the people settled the islands in the Nevos Sea and also, at one point were the rulers briefly after the Great War conquered Darba and many of them live in the sort of swamp slums now.
